title: Algorithm coverage: RSA-PSS, Ed25519, P-521, legacy SHA-1
description:
Expand DefaultVerifier to cover the algorithms found in real-world PKIs. Without RSA-PSS and Ed25519, the library cannot validate chains from Let's Encrypt ISRG Root X2, government PKIs, or modern CAs. Existing epic PKIX-qws tracks the 4 individual algorithms. This is the single feature addition that most expands the set of certificate chains the library can validate.

Subtasks (from PKIX-qws):
- RSA-PSS-SHA256 SignatureVerifier
- Ed25519 SignatureVerifier  
- ECDSA P-521 + SHA-512 SignatureVerifier
- Legacy SHA-1 RSA+ECDSA (feature-gated, off by default)

Acceptance: cargo test against a corpus of real-world chains from CT logs covering each algorithm.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-11-25, same day: the SHA-1 aside in this bead closure was wrong.

It said PKIX-qws.4 "must not be actioned" because "SHA-1 is refused by design". That was my inference from DefaultVerifier having no SHA-1 backend, not a decision anyone made, and it contradicts the repository own docs -- PKIX README:227 reads "legacy SHA-1 (feature-gated, off by default, for validating old chains)" and :311 lists it as a P1.

Confirmed stance: VERIFY-ONLY, OPT-IN, OFF BY DEFAULT. PKIX-qws.4 is real work and remains open. Nothing signs with SHA-1 and nothing should, so there is no "create" side; the opt-in feature should sit outside the `rustcrypto` umbrella so that umbrella stays "algorithms we recommend".

Everything else in this closure stands -- RSA-PSS, Ed25519 and P-521 are implemented and the defaults are fixed. Only the SHA-1 sentence was false.
close_reason:
STALE -- the algorithms this describes are implemented, and the real remaining work (the defaults) is now done too. Closed under PKIX-dzjn.

Evidence, verified rather than assumed: pkix-path/src/verifiers.rs dispatches RSA-PSS (OID_RSASSA_PSS, verifiers.rs:74, used at :304/:399/:505), Ed25519 (OID_ED25519, :90, used at :537) and ECDSA P-521 (OID_SECP521R1, :59, dispatched :213). The rustcrypto umbrella feature is rsa + p256 + p384 + p521 + ed25519.

What was genuinely missing was not implementation but DEFAULTS: pkix-path had default = ["rsa", "p256"], so a caller who did nothing got a verifier that rejected a P-384 chain as unsupported_key -- correct behaviour, baffling default. Fixed in 758ce9f1: default = ["rustcrypto"], shipped as pkix-path 0.4.2.

That change had a consequence worth recording here, because it is the kind of thing a future reader of these beads will hit. ed25519 pulls ed25519-dalek, hence curve25519-dalek, whose build script selects an x86 SIMD backend that fails on x86_64-unknown-none with "rustc-LLVM ERROR: Do not know how to split the result of this operator!" -- the same error the bare-metal CI job already worked around for sha2. Fixed in 2a33baf5 by extending that flag list rather than weakening the gate; thumbv7em and riscv64 were unaffected. pkix-path Cargo.toml documents the flags for consumers building that target.

The regulated-environment half is also done and tested (dd45bada): an algorithm a build will not perform surfaces as SignatureNotVerified { reason: UnsupportedAlgorithm }, distinct from SignatureInvalid, all the way out through pkix_chain::Error. Four tests in pkix-chain/tests/regulated_algorithms.rs cover UnsupportedAlgorithm, UnsupportedKey, MalformedKey and the negative case.

PKIX-qws.4 (legacy SHA-1 verifiers) is deliberately NOT closed by this and must not be actioned: SHA-1 is refused by design.
